notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 69% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 58:05 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 55:05 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Evgeni Malkin is expected back after missing 1 game.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

story.head: Clifton returns to Pittsburgh
paras: The Penguins are winless in three (0-2-1), while the Bruins have won two in a row. Going in, the Bruins are first in the Atlantic (fourth in the NHL) and the Pens seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th).

The Bruins’ record (.719) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.555), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Penguins have played better than their record (.400) says: their chances are worth about .568, mostly because they’re 3-6 in one-goal games. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). Boston has allowed 2.38 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Penguins, they sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest) and rarely throw hits (lowest). They also get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd), so the Penguins have the edge over the Bruins on shots from in close. The Bruins could find some good looks against the Penguins, who give up plenty of them.

David Pastrňák (8 G / 12 A / 20 P in 16 GP) leads the Bruins in scoring. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Evgeni Malkin (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Jeremy Swayman (8-3-1 / .912 SV% in 12 GS) has been outstanding for Boston and is expected to start. Artūrs Šilovs (5-4-1 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh.
